title: Reading Rates Off a Sparse Term Structure
body:
A fixed-income desk only has quotes for a few bond maturities. It keeps them as N knots: a maturity T[i] in years and the annual rate Y[i] in percent quoted for it. The knots are sorted by maturity, strictly increasing.

Traders ask for rates at other maturities, and every request Q[j] is answered the same way:

  • On a knot (Q[j] = T[i]): the rate is Y[i].
  • Between two knots (T[i] < Q[j] < T[i+1]): read it off the straight line through those two knots, Y[i] + (Y[i+1] − Y[i]) · (Q[j] − T[i]) / (T[i+1] − T[i]).
  • Outside the quoted range: before the first knot the rate stays at Y[0]; after the last knot it stays at Y[N−1]. The lines are never extended past the ends.

Answer the M requests in the order they were asked.

Function to complete

Complete ratesAt(maturities, rates, queries). It returns the rate for each request, in request order (printed with 4 decimals).

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: N. The next N lines: T[i] and Y[i]. Then a line with M, and a line with the M requests Q[j]. Every T, Y and Q has exactly two digits after the decimal point.
out: M rates on one line, separated by spaces, each rounded to exactly 4 digits after the decimal point.
cons: 0.00 ≤ Q[j] ≤ 60.00; requests come in any order and can repeat
No exact answer lies exactly halfway between two 4-decimal values, so ordinary rounding (%.4f) is enough

samples.ex: 1.50 sits halfway between the knots (1.00, 4.50) and (2.00, 4.80), so the rate is 4.50 + 0.30 × 0.5 = 4.65. 6.00 is past the last knot (5.00), so it takes that knot's rate, 5.20.

0.25 comes before the first knot, so it takes 3.10. 2.00 is a knot: 3.70. 4.50 is halfway from 2.00 to 7.00: 3.70 + 0.50 × 0.5 = 3.95. 8.50 is halfway from 7.00 to 10.00: 4.20 − 0.15 × 0.5 = 4.125. 12.00 is past the last knot: 4.05.
The curve can fall too: 2.00 is halfway, so 6.00 − 1.00 × 0.5 = 5.50. The other two requests are the knots themselves. Answers follow the order of the requests, not of the maturities.

spec.returns: the rate for each request, in request order (printed with 4 decimals)

wrong.why: extends the end segments as straight lines instead of holding the end rates
sorts the requests to sweep them once, then answers in maturity order

if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    _n = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    maturities = []; rates = []
    for _ in range((_n)):
        maturities.append(float(_t[_p + 0]))
        rates.append(float(_t[_p + 1]))
        _p += 2
    _m = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    queries = list(map(float, _t[_p:_p + (_m)])); _p += (_m)
    _r = Solution().ratesAt(maturities, rates, queries)
    print(" ".join("%.4f" % _x for _x in _r))
